title: The suno pile counts scout takes as decided
body:
## Summary
lib/ledger/v1/sources/suno.ts weirOf excluded scout takes from pending but counted them in decided.

## Description
`decided: s.clips.length - pending.length` (lib/ledger/v1/sources/suno.ts weirOf) while pending filtered `!isScoutSunoJob`. mv.ts and sound.ts count decided over the pending population. Fixed: both over non-scout clips.

## Flow
- a scout night's takes land in suno.json unjudged
- Floor/Runs read the suno pile
- decided included every scout take

## Expected impact
The suno triage pile's decided count is now the triaged own clips. Nothing else reads the field differently.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - decided counts only the pile's own clips
Before: decided 4, pending 1 (2 own clips, 3 scout)
After: decided 1, pending 1
Method: gate - v1-suno.test.ts red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Article reader swallows a job-list failure as 'no holder'
body:
## Summary
heldByJobs returned an empty set when the kernel job list failed, so held article runs read as stalled.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sources/articles.ts heldByJobs: `if (!jobs.ok) return new Set()`. Every job-held run became driving:false -> interrupted with STALLED's resume prompt. Now heldIn(store): Result and readArticles fails with the store's words.

## Flow
- kernel job list read fails
- readArticles marks job-held runs not driving
- Runs draws them interrupted and offers Resume

## Expected impact
Runs shows the articles source as a gap with its error rather than prompting a second drive.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed holder read is an error, not an empty holder set
Before: read ok, held run driving:false
After: read err 'articles: the kernel's job list could not be read: ...'
Method: gate - v1-articles.test.ts over a closed kernel, red with the swallow restored
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Turn reader's cap kept a random 2000, not the newest
body:
## Summary
readTurns cut with ids.sort().slice(-2000) though turn ids are random hex.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sources/turns.ts readTurns copied clips.ts's lexical cut; clip ids are time-ordered (mintClipId), turn ids random (lib/turns/ledger.ts mintTurnId). Past the cap it now keeps the most recently written by mtime.

## Flow
- more than 2000 turn records exist
- reader keeps lexically last 2000
- a live turn can fall out of Runs and the ledger

## Expected impact
Live and recent turns survive the cap; under the cap nothing changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the cap keeps the newest records
Before: cap 2 over 3: newest dropped
After: the 2 newest kept
Method: gate - v1-turns.test.ts, red on the lexical cut
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Three header counts disagree with what they count
body:
## Summary
facts.ts 'eleven sources', packet.ts 'Seven are the same word', roots.ts 'Four v1 stores' with a stale strips line.

## Description
V1_SOURCES holds 15; WEIR_TO_PACKET 8 of 10 same-word; roots.ts listed 5 stores incl. strips, which uses stripsRoot() since L33.

## Flow
- read each header count
- count the code
- replace with the walk or the true statement

## Expected impact
Readers no longer act on a stale strips root claim.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - prose matches code
Before: 3 of 3 counts false
After: 0 false
Method: probe - counted against the code
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Sound verdict key omits judgedAt, so a flip-back verdict is lost
body:
## Summary
sound.ts keys a verdict `verdict.<value>` though v1 records judgedAt; forge/extract/strips key by value AND instant.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sources/sound.ts eventsOf: `f.recorded(t.id, `verdict.${t.verdict}`, t.judgedAt, ...)`. A take judged kept, then rejected, then kept again: the third verdict's key is already held (from t1) -> appendOnce reports drift and appends nothing; the ledger's latest verdict says rejected while the store says kept. Fix: `verdict.${verdict}.${judgedAt}`; but that re-keys every already-held sound verdict, appending one duplicate verdict per judged take on the next sync.

## Flow
- judge kept, sync
- judge rejected, sync
- judge kept, sync: drifted=1, appended=0

## Expected impact
The ledger would carry every verdict change; the cost is one duplicate per already-judged take unless the worker keeps the old key for a verdict whose judgedAt equals the held row's.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every verdict change reaches the ledger
Before: flip-back: 0 of 1 recorded (walked from appendOnce same-key semantics)
After: 1 of 1 predicted
Method: simulation - three-verdict sequence walked; the round did not take the store-copy figure for the re-key cost
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a v1-sound.test.ts case syncing kept(t1)->rejected(t2)->kept(t3) into an in-memory kernel: the ledger's last verdict for the take; plus a re-sync over a store copy counting the one-time duplicate verdict rows a re-key appends

title: Runs' live read builds every source's full event projection
body:
## Summary
liveJobs calls each source's project(), which digests every log line and builds all events, only to read live/weir/slots/holds.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts liveJobs -> readAll -> src.project(snapshot, ctx): forge/extract/dojo f.logged digests each log line (lib/ledger/v1/facts.ts logged), for up to 500 runs per source, on every Runs render. The events are discarded.

## Flow
- open Runs
- liveNow reads and projects 15 sources
- events array built and dropped

## Expected impact
Runs renders faster on a box with many runs; risk is a second projection path that drifts from project().

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - Runs' live read does no event work
Before: unmeasured: digests per call = sum of log lines over <=500 runs per source
After: 0 digests
Method: simulation - read of the call path; no timing taken in-round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: time liveJobs(V1_SOURCES) over a copy of foundry-out runs/extract (GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH temp) and count sha256 digests computed per call, A = project() as today, B = a live-only projection path

title: A muse-wing read failure hides the scout wing's nights and seeds
body:
## Summary
scout.ts and seeds.ts read both wings and fail the whole source if either wing fails.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sources/scout.ts read: `if (!muse.ok) return muse;` after a good scout read; seeds.ts read: Promise.all over SCOUT_WINGS in one try. An unreadable muse root removes the morning scout pile from the Floor. The repo's rule elsewhere is 'a failed listing fails the source' (forge.ts read), so whether a wing is a listing or a record is a semantics call the worker must pin with a test.

## Flow
- muse root unreadable
- scout source read fails
- pkt:scout:<night> pile disappears from the Weir

## Expected impact
The scout wing stays visible when only muse fails; the muse failure is an ingest.skip.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one wing failing does not hide the other
Before: scout pile 0 when muse fails (walked)
After: scout pile 1, muse skip recorded
Method: simulation - walked read(); no failing-root fixture built in round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: v1-scout/scout-muse-readers case: withWing('muse') listNights throws EACCES -> does projectScout still carry the scout night's Weir pile; same for seedsSource

title: Turn media table names 6 of 17 turn classes; the rest default to video
body:
## Summary
turns.ts MEDIA maps 6 turn classes; research, repair, probe, edit-plan, compose and 6 more fall to 'video'.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sources/turns.ts MEDIA vs lib/text/types.ts TurnClass (15) + lib/turns/ledger.ts WorkTurn (2). Typing it Record<TurnClass|WorkTurn, MediaLane> makes a new class a compile error, but which medium research/repair/probe belong to is a product call.

## Flow
- a research turn runs
- Runs draws it on the video media lane

## Expected impact
Each turn class draws on a lane someone chose.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every turn class has an explicit medium
Before: 6 of 17 explicit
After: 17 of 17
Method: probe - counted the union against the table
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
